title: Cyclone Akvan to bring heavy rain to coastal Bengal on Thursday and Friday; signal raised at Kolkata port
dek: The Kolkata weather office forecasts heavy rain in the 24 Parganas and Midnapore districts from 19 November, and thunderstorms with lightning across south Bengal, though the storm will cross the coast in Andhra Pradesh.
author: Declaration Desk
body:
Heavy rain is likely at one or two places in North and South 24 Parganas and East and West Midnapore on Thursday, 19 November, and in South 24 Parganas, East and West Midnapore, Jhargram and Bankura on Friday, as Cyclonic Storm Akvan moves north over the Bay of Bengal, the Regional Meteorological Centre (RMC) in Kolkata said in a special bulletin issued at 1 pm on Tuesday. Thunderstorms with lightning and gusty winds of 30-40 kmph are likely across south Bengal on both days, and Kolkata and Howrah are expected to get light to moderate rain from Wednesday.

The storm's centre is forecast to cross the Andhra Pradesh coast, hundreds of kilometres south-west of Bengal, around noon on Friday. Distant Warning Signal No. 2 has been hoisted at the Kolkata and Haldia docks of Hooghly port, the RMC said, with sectional signals at Sagar Island.

## Latest forecast

According to the RMC bulletin, south Bengal stays dry until Wednesday morning. From 8.30 am on Wednesday, light to moderate rain or thundershowers are likely at a few places in North 24 Parganas, South 24 Parganas, East Midnapore, West Midnapore, Kolkata and Howrah. On Thursday rain is very likely at many places in those districts and in Jhargram and Bankura, with heavy rain of 7-11 cm at one or two places in the four coastal and near-coastal districts. On Friday rain is expected at many places across south Bengal, with heavy falls in South 24 Parganas, East and West Midnapore, Jhargram and Bankura, and on Saturday heavy rain is likely at one or two places in Purulia as the storm's remnants move inland. Light to moderate showers are forecast at a few places across south Bengal until 24 November.

The RMC warned of lightning strikes, especially in open fields, temporary waterlogging in low-lying areas and underpasses on 19 and 20 November, and some damage to standing crops and horticulture, and advised people not to shelter under trees or electric poles during thunderstorms. North Bengal is expected to stay largely dry, with light rain at one or two places in Darjeeling, Kalimpong and Jalpaiguri until Wednesday morning and in Malda and the two Dinajpurs from 21 November.

There is no fishermen's warning for the West Bengal coast itself, the RMC said, but fishermen have been told not to go into the deep sea of the northwest Bay of Bengal adjoining the west-central Bay from 17 to 20 November, and those already at sea have been asked to return. Squally winds of 45-55 kmph gusting to 65 kmph are expected there, rising to 50-60 kmph gusting to 70 kmph from Thursday morning, with rough to very rough seas.

In its 6.15 pm national bulletin on Tuesday, the India Meteorological Department (IMD) said the storm had barely moved during the day and lay about 590 km east of Chennai at 2.30 pm, and kept its forecast of light to moderate rain at many places in Gangetic West Bengal, with heavy rain at isolated places, on 19 and 20 November.

## For the fishing fleets

The forecast winds and rough seas over the northwest Bay matter for the trawler fleets of Digha, Kakdwip, Namkhana and Frasergunj, which work these waters.

## A brief end to the chill

The weather system is also expected to push temperatures up. Darjeeling was the coldest place in Bengal on Sunday at 8.2°C, and Kolkata's minimum was 21.3°C, according to reports. Day and night temperatures across south Bengal are expected to rise by 2-3°C from 18 November as moist winds from the Bay arrive, the reports said, citing the weather office.

## Why it matters for Bengal

Rain in the second half of November comes as the aman paddy crop, south Bengal's main rice crop, approaches harvest, and as potato planting begins in districts such as Hooghly and Paschim Medinipur; heavy rain at this stage can flatten ripe paddy and waterlog fields. Bengal escaped the worst of Cyclone Arnab and Cyclone Murasu, which hit Andhra Pradesh and Odisha in late October and early November.

## What happens next

The RMC in Kolkata issues district warnings for Bengal and updates its special bulletins as the storm moves; the IMD issues national bulletins every three hours while the cyclone is active. The state government has not announced any special measures for the storm. The Declaration will update this story as forecasts for Bengal are revised.
